entries.name: GUB-UCN2
entries.summary: GUB-UCN2 is an investigational subcutaneous urocortin-2 analogue and selective CRHR2 agonist. Gubra reported on 28 July 2026 that the first participant had completed the first visit in a three-part Phase 1/2a study. The sponsor-submitted registry records a recruiting study with an actual 27 July 2026 start, approximately 188 planned participants, and monotherapy and incretin-combination cohorts. Muscle volume and muscle function are planned study endpoints.
entries.ukAuthorisation: The reviewed evidence does not establish UK marketing authorisation for GUB-UCN2, alone or in combination.
entries.nhsEngland: No NICE recommendation or NHS England access is established by this early research.
entries.supply: Clinical development in Germany does not establish lawful UK retail supply, pharmacy stock or sale by Shift Some Timber.
entries.limitations: Recruitment, first visit and an actual study start are not efficacy or safety results. The 188-participant enrolment and December 2028 completion remain estimates, and the registry has no posted results. Muscle-volume, muscle-function and combination cohorts are planned research, not demonstrated preservation, improved function or added benefit. All reported fat-mass, lean-mass, cardiac, renal and metabolic effects in the 28 July announcement are preclinical, not human findings. The evidence establishes no approved dose, UK authorisation, NICE or NHS access, UK supply or clinical approval.

entries.name: MBL949
entries.stage: Phase 2 trial terminated early; obesity development not continued
entries.summary: The sponsor-submitted NCT05199090 record and Novartis patient summary describe a 126-participant Phase 2 obesity study that started in February 2022 and ended early in May 2023. Novartis says the observed tolerability-to-benefit balance was not favourable at the studied doses and that it decided not to continue studying MBL949 in obesity.
entries.ukAuthorisation: The reviewed evidence does not establish UK marketing authorisation for MBL949.
entries.nhsEngland: No NICE recommendation or NHS England access is established. A stopped research programme is not an NHS treatment option.
entries.supply: The reviewed evidence does not establish lawful UK retail supply, pharmacy stock or sale by Shift Some Timber.
entries.limitations: The registry labels the study terminated and includes posted results, but this concise Watch entry does not independently reanalyse its efficacy or adverse-event tables. Novartis's patient summary says the early-stop decision was not related to the safety of MBL949 while also stating that the effect on weight loss was insufficient given the number of adverse events; both statements are retained without turning them into a broader safety conclusion. This programme must not be presented as active, authorised or supplied, and its outcome does not establish conclusions about other GDF15-pathway candidates.
